- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>

</commentary>

</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

## ac642cf1-e1c8-4490-9caa-814476453870
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
- upstream-sync-review: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
- agent-sdk-dev:new-sdk-app: Create and setup a new Claude Agent SDK application
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- commit-commands:clean_gone: Cleans up all git branches marked as [gone] (branches that have been deleted on the remote but still exist locally), including removing associated worktrees.
- commit-commands:commit-push-pr: Commit, push, and open a PR
- commit-commands:commit: Create a git commit
- feature-dev:feature-dev: Guided feature development with codebase understanding and architecture focus
- plugin-dev:create-plugin: Guided end-to-end plugin creation workflow with component design, implementation, and validation
- pr-review-toolkit:review-pr: Comprehensive PR review using specialized agents
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- vercel:bootstrap: Bootstrap a repository with Vercel-linked resources by running preflight checks, provisioning integrations, verifying env keys, and then executing db/dev startup commands safely.
- vercel:deploy: Deploy the current project to Vercel. Pass "prod" or "production" as argument to deploy to production. Default is preview deployment.
- vercel:env: Manage Vercel environment variables. Commands include list, pull, add, remove, and diff. Use to sync environment variables between Vercel and your local development environment.
- vercel:status: Show the status of the current Vercel project — recent deployments, linked project info, and environment overview.
- claude-code-setup:claude-automation-recommender: Analyze a codebase and recommend Claude Code automations (hooks, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers). Use when user asks for automation recommendations, wants to optimize their Claude Code setup, mentions improving Claude Code workflows, asks how to first set up Claude Code for a project, or wants to know what Claude Code features they should use.
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. === PR #68 FULL ===
#68 SFCC-194: Was/Now sale price on PDP with variant-scoped pricing (PRC-09)
branch: feature/SFCC-194_pdp-was-now-price → develop
author: joselitopperezjr-acn
created: 2026-08-27T09:13:28Z  updated: 2026-08-27T10:52:31Z
diff: +415/-118 across 13 files

--- BODY ---
## Summary

- Introduces `ZimmProductPrice` atom (PRC-09) that renders a single formatted price in the default state and a two-span Was/Now treatment when `originalPrice` is supplied. Styling lives in a co-located `zimmProductPrice.css.ts` recipe with `default` and `sale` multi-part variants; the `sale` variant switches the container to a flex row, mutes the Was span, and highlights the Now span in success green.
- Extends `ZimmProductContent` molecule to accept and forward `originalPrice` and `isPriceLoading` props to `ZimmProductPrice`, keeping the molecule's existing composition contract intact.
- Adds `selectPdpProductInfo` mapper (`pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts`) that derives `wasPrice` from `getPriceData`'s `listPrice` only when `isOnSale` is true and the list price is a real number — the Was/Now atoms branch entirely on presence of this value, so a missing or expired sale in BM correctly reverts to single-price display on next render.
- Implements variant-scoped pricing in `pages/product-detail/index.tsx` using the master product's `variants[]` as the authoritative `tieredPrices` source across three URL states: no selection (falls through to base `priceData`), colour-only (`?color=`), and colour+size (`?pid=`). A `masterProductRef` caches the master on first load so the correct `tieredPrices` are available after SFCC switches the fetched product to a standalone variant.
- Adds a deep-link fallback for shoppers arriving with `?pid=` already set on a fresh page load (no prior master fetch), using the standalone variant's own `tieredPrices` from `perPricebook: true` when `masterProductRef` is empty.
- Guards against stale Was/Now during variant re-fetches via `isPriceStale` (`requestedProductId !== product?.id`), suppressing the price entirely while `keepPreviousData` holds the previous variant's data.
- Fixes `aria-hidden` being set on the `ZimmProductPrice` live region during the loading state — removing it would prevent screen readers from registering the region before the price arrives, breaking WCAG 2.2 AA 4.1.3 announcement on settlement.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npm run test` — all tests passing including 8 new `ZimmProductPrice` unit tests and updated `productInfo` tests
- [x] CodeRabbit CLI review — 0 findings (`coderabbit review --agent --base develop`)
- [x] PRC-09 criteria verified: sale product shows Was/Now; non-sale product shows single price; currency formats correctly per storefront; Was/Now clears when sale is removed in BM
- [x] Variant-scoped pricing verified across all three URL states: no selection, colour-only, colour+size
- [x] Deep-link scenario (`?pid=` on fresh load) handled via standalone variant `tieredPrices` fallback

content.content:
=== pdp.md lines 35-70 ===

- **Coming Soon** — product is displayed on PDP before stock is added or purchase is enabled
- **Back in Soon** — product has sold out but will restock imminently (re-cut)
- **Unavailable (size-level)** — triggers the Notify Me flow for the affected size variant
- OOS sizes visually greyed out/disabled; Add to Bag is suppressed for that size variant (PRD-014)
- All product states (Coming Soon, Back in Soon, Unavailable) must comply with **Google Merchant Centre** feed rules — ineligible-state products must not surface in product feeds (PRD-017)
- Low-stock indicator at size level: displays **"LOW"** label — purely visual, does not alter CTA behaviour or block add-to-bag (PRD-012; also PRD-030 from CAI)

---

## 5. Pricing Display

- Display price in storefront currency (AUD, USD, GBP, EUR)
- Sale pricing: was/now format (PRD-003, confirmed — subject to designs). If price changes again after being put on sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042, confirmed)
- Tax label per storefront: GST (AU), VAT (UK/EU), Tax (US) (PAY, confirmed)
- **Duties and taxes information** displayed country-specifically on PDP (PRD-013, confirmed)
- **DDP/DDU messaging** displayed on PDP per applicable countries (PAY-059, confirmed)
- Max configurable purchase quantity enforced per customer group (PRD-011, confirmed)
- *Open: HK/ME/US Intl/EU Intl pricing display — Global-e pricing via SFCC price books is defined and REG-041 is confirmed (REG-040 retired). Sign-off of the full mechanism (PRC-34..PRC-43) is still pending; do not implement until confirmed.*

---

## 6. Availability & Add to Bag

*Buffer stock rules apply on PDP. See [cart.md](cart.md) section 5 for the full buffer stock system.*

- Per-size availability shown (ADD TO BAG / OUT OF STOCK / low-stock "LOW" indicator)
- **ADD TO BAG** shown when quantity is above buffer threshold
- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when quantity is at or below buffer threshold (back-in-stock capture presented)
- Low-stock indicator at size level — no quantity number shown — displays "LOW" label
- **Max 3 units per SKU** (same size + colour) enforced at add-to-cart (CAI-017, confirmed)
- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart (CAI-032, confirmed)

---

## 7. Primary CTAs & Supporting Links (PRD-018 – PRD-022, confirmed)

================================================
=== pricing-currency-globale.md §3 (lines 28-80) ===
- Bulk assignment of tax class to products supported — tax class driven by AP21 taxonomy ID (derived from product category, configured by finance) fed into SFCC via MuleSoft; no manual bulk updates required. Avalara covers AU, EU, US, and UK domestic storefronts for go-live. International storefronts (HK, ME, US Int'l, EU Int'l) handled through Global-e. HS code handling may still need further exploration but is not a go-live blocker (PRC-07, confirmed — signed off by Emma/Rebecca 2026-06-24)
- Product prices displayed consistently in storefront currency across PLP, PDP, mini-bag, cart, wishlist, recommended tiles, and checkout (PRC-08, PRC-33)

---

## 3. Sale & Markdown Pricing (PRC-09 – PRC-13)

- Original list price displayed alongside active sale price — shown on PLP tiles, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, wishlist, recommended tiles, and order history. Note (DR): sale items are usually excluded from recommendations via a manual rule (PRC-09)
- Business users can schedule sale pricing to go live at a specified future date and time. Category pre-merchandised; team QCs via live-preview before go-live (PRC-10, confirmed)
- **SFCC native storefront preview** supports QC of scheduled pricing and category changes before go-live, including preview for specific customer groups — scoped to SFCC OOTB preview, no custom build (PRC-11, confirmed)
- Final sale flag supported on products (PRC-12, confirmed). Assumption: `is_returnable` drives returnable status, `final_sale` drives front-end final-sale messaging. Attribute distinction and AP21 derivation still to be confirmed — see Open Items. No final-sale icon in design yet
- Price display behaviour based on AP21 `MarkdownStatus` values (permanent / temporary / temppermanent) — open: Zimmermann to confirm what each value means and what storefront behaviour it should drive (PRC-13, open)

---

## 4. Multi-Currency & Regional Pricebooks (PRC-14, PRC-36 – PRC-43, PRC-47 – PRC-52)

- Country/currency selector shows prices in the currency configured for the customer's selected shipping country (PRC-14, confirmed). Note (RJ): the country selector is not present on the AU site
- **Country-to-currency mapping** configurable in SFCC Business Manager without code deployment (PRC-36, PRC-52)
- Per currency, the system stores the **conversion approach**: (a) Base RRP, (b) Fixed Pricelist from AP21, (c) Fixed FX rate from base, or (d) Dynamic FX rate from base (PRC-37)
- **Nightly job** loads Global-e pricing into SFCC: FX rates, price coefficients, and rounding rules (PRC-38)
- Pricebooks generated from Global-e pricing data and imported into SFCC (PRC-39)
- Target-currency price calculation: `base pricebook price × FX rate × country coefficient × product-class coefficient` (PRC-40)
- Calculated prices included in the SFCC search index for price-based filters and sort on PLP/search (PRC-41)
- All promotion calculations executed in the customer's selected ship-to currency (PRC-42)
- **Currency display formatting** per locale: symbol position, decimal places (including zero-decimal currencies), thousand separator, minus-sign for refunds (PRC-47)
- **FX rate locked at order placement** and applied to any refund at the same locked rate — refund in target currency equals original charged amount (PRC-48)
- **Currency rounding strategy** per currency (e.g. nearest whole AED, 2 decimal EUR, 0 decimal JPY); applied at line-item level before tax/promotion stacking (PRC-49)
- Business Manager interface for authorised users: view conversion approach per currency, set/change conversion approach, view current FX rate with last-updated timestamp and feed status; read-only access for merchandising team (PRC-50)
- Bulk import/export of currency config via SFCC Site Import/Export, OCAPI, or deployment scripts — technical users only (PRC-51)

---

## 5. VIC & Customer Group Pricing (PRC-17 – PRC-19)

Customer-group-specific catalogue pricing — visible on PLP, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, recommended tiles, wishlist (not cart-only discounts). Discounts do not apply to products already on sale or to gift cards.

| Customer group | Discount |
|---|---|
| Gold VIC | Permanent 10% off all non-sale products |
| Platinum VIC | Permanent discount — rate TBC (Zimmermann to confirm) |
| VIC early access | Flat 30% off before public sale goes live; removed before public sale |
| Advent customers | e.g. 50% off during Advent events |
| PR companies and investors | Configured discount |

- **Customer group discounts do NOT stack on sale items** (PRC-18, revised per DR): sale items are excluded from promotion set-ups. Example: a Gold VIC customer receives 10% off full-price items, but if they add a sale product to cart they get the sale price only — no extra 10% on top. The system must continue to support this exclusion.
- Configurable priority rules in SFCC Business Manager (e.g. Gold VIC 10% excludes gift cards and items already on sale) (PRC-19)

---

## 6. Global-e Pricing & Cart Handoff (PRC-15 – PRC-16, PRC-43 – PRC-46, PRC-53 – PRC-55)

- DDP/DDU duties messaging on PDP per country — configurable per country (PRC-15)

# SFCC-194 — PDP – Was/Now Sale Price

> Working reference for PR #68. Compiled 2026-08-28 from Jira, Confluence, and `.docs/`.
> Temporary scratch file — not part of the repo.

---

## 1. At a glance

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Key** | SFCC-194 ([open](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-194)) |
| **Summary** | PDP – Was/Now Sale Price |
| **Type / Priority** | Story / **High** |
| **Status** | In Progress |
| **Parent epic** | **SFCC-5 — Product Detail Page (PDP)** ⚠️ see §7.1 |
| **Sprint** | SFCC Sprint 4 (active, 25 Aug → 07 Sep 2026) |
| **Story points** | 2 |
| **Assignee** | Jersey Perez Jr (joselito.perez.jr@accenture.com) |
| **Reporter** | Jasmijn Tsang |
| **Labels** | `Custom`, `PRC-09`, `PRD-003`, `Squad-A` |
| **Created / Updated** | 2026-07-20 / 2026-08-28 |
| **Implementing PR** | [#68](https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pull/68) — `feature/SFCC-194_pdp-was-now-price` → `develop` |

**Sprint 4 goal:** *"Advance PDP feature build-out and complete the GlobalLink translation cartridge setup end-to-end, while closing out Sprint 3 carryover QA (Header, Footer, PDP Static Product Info) and kicking off Adyen checkout integration."*

---

## 2. User story

> **As a** Shopper,
> **I want** to see both the original and sale price clearly displayed on the PDP when a product is on sale,
> **so that** I can understand the discount before deciding to buy.

### Description (verbatim)

> When a product has an active sale price in SFCC (driven by a sale pricebook), the PDP displays both the original price (Was) and the sale price (Now). The sale price takes visual prominence. When no sale price is active, only the standard price is displayed. Price display is consistent across all storefronts with appropriate currency formatting per region.
>
> **This story covers the PDP price display only. Pricebook configuration and sale pricebook management are out of scope.**

Image reference is attached, but the ticket states **"Figma is leading"**.

---

## 3. Acceptance Criteria (verbatim, 4)

| # | Criterion |
|---|---|
| **AC1** | Given a product has an active sale price, when the PDP renders, then **both the original price (Was) and sale price (Now) are displayed with the sale price visually prominent**. |
| **AC2** | Given a product has **no active sale price**, when the PDP renders, then **only the standard price is displayed** and no Was/Now treatment is applied. |
| **AC3** | Given the shopper is on **any storefront**, when prices display, then the **correct currency and formatting** applies for that region. |
| **AC4** | Given a sale price is **removed or expired in BM**, when the next page render occurs, then the Was/Now display is removed and only the standard price shows. |

### AC observations

- **All four are display-only.** Nothing in the ACs mentions variant selection, colour/size switching, URL state, deep-linking, or loading/stale behaviour. See §8 for how this compares to what PR #68 actually implements.
- **AC3 is the widest one.** "Any storefront" = 8 SFCC sites / 6 regions / 11 locales. Currency formatting rules are specified in **PRC-47** (symbol position, decimal places incl. zero-decimal currencies, thousand separator, minus placement) — the AC does not restate them, so PRC-47 is the real yardstick.
- **AC4 is a negative/expiry case** — worth confirming how it is actually being verified (BM change + re-render), since it depends on SFCC data, not front-end logic.
- **No accessibility AC.** Compare SFCC-737, which carries explicit a11y criteria (focus order, heading level, WCAG 2.1 AA). PR #68 does address a live-region/`aria-hidden` concern, but there is no AC to verify it against. See §10-F.

---

## 4. Design

### 4.1 Reference image (attached to the ticket)

`image-20260814-042632.png` — uploaded by Jasmijn Tsang, 2026-08-14. Shows:

```
INDRA PLUNGE HALTER MAXI DRESS
Was $1,100   Now $1,000
```

- "Was $1,100" rendered **greyed out / muted — no strikethrough visible**
- "Now $1,000" rendered in the darker, prominent treatment
- Both sit on one line, directly beneath the product name and above the description

### 4.2 Approved decision

Comment from **Dani Rivett**, 2026-08-14:

> "Rebecca has approved the green sale price with the greyed out Was price."

This closed subtask **SFCC-215** — *"Was/Now pricing – Share feedback on greying out the 'was' price and ask to see a few options, green colour not 100% agreed either"* (assignee Dani Rivett, now **Done**). So the green Now / greyed Was treatment is the signed-off direction.

### 4.3 Figma

Two distinct files — do not cross-compare measurements between them:

| File | Link |
|---|---|
| **Design System 2026** (component inventory root) | [wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm](https://www.figma.com/design/wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/Zimmermann_Design_System_2026?node-id=40000730-13662) |
| **Design Workspace** (Was/Now row in 04.2 tracker) | [XWz3ItpkSqL45P5IFOnQgB, node 1800-58176](https://www.figma.com/design/XWz3ItpkSqL45P5IFOnQgB/Design-Workspace?node-id=1800-58176) |

### 4.4 ⚠️ Three-way inconsistency on the "Was" treatment

| Source | Says |
|---|---|
| Jira attachment (SFCC-194) | Was is **greyed out**, no strikethrough |
| Approved comment (Dani/Rebecca) | "**greyed out** Was price" + **green** Now |
| Confluence **04.2 Design Tracker** | "Was/now **strikethrough** price across all surfaces" |
| Sibling story **SFCC-778** ACs | "**strikethrough** original price, promotional price highlighted" (×2 ACs) |

Grey-out and strikethrough are different visual treatments. SFCC-194 is being built to grey-out; the downstream story it blocks (SFCC-778) specifies strikethrough. **Unless deliberate, these will diverge into two different price components.** Worth resolving before SFCC-778 starts.

> Note: 04.2 is the *page-level* tracker and is known to lag; **04.7 / 04.72 are the live component-level trackers**. But SFCC-778's ACs are current, so the conflict is real regardless of 04.2's staleness.

### 4.5 Design lock status (Confluence 04.7 Component Inventory)

There is **no standalone "Price" component** in the inventory. Price is a nested element of:

```
Module: PDP Hero              🟡 Done, minor update required
  ↳ Sub-component: Product Content   🟡 Done, minor update required   ← price lives here
```

So the price treatment is **not independently design-locked** — it inherits Product Content's "minor update required" state. Per **04.72**: *"user stories cannot be written, reviewed or signed off until the relevant design components are locked."*

---

## 5. Scope

### In scope (per the story)
- PDP price display only
- Was + Now rendering when a sale pricebook entry is active
- Single standard price when not on sale
- Correct currency + formatting per storefront
- Reverting to single price when the sale is removed/expired in BM

### Out of scope (explicit in the story)
- Pricebook configuration
- Sale pricebook management

### Out of scope (inherited from epic SFCC-5)
- Product attribute / data model config → SFCC-4
- Sorting and filtering → SFCC-6, SFCC-7
- Inventory list setup and reservation → SFCC-11
- **Pricing display logic and pricebook setup → SFCC-18** ⚠️ see §7.1
- Contentful content authoring
- MuleSoft / AP21 feed development

---

## 6. Requirement traceability

| Req ID | Source | Statement | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PRC-09** | Confluence 04.1.12 | "The system will display the original list price alongside the active sale price when a sale pricebook entry is active; this will appear on **product tiles (PLP), PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, wishlist, recommended product tiles and order history**." Owner Accenture · ALL storefronts · **Custom** | Confirmed |
| **PRD-003** | `.docs/prd/pdp.md:48` | "Sale pricing: was/now format (PRD-003, confirmed — subject to designs)." | Confirmed, *subject to designs* |
| **REG-042** | `.docs/prd/pdp.md:48`, `regional.md:99`, `plp.md:50` | "**If price changes again after being put on sale, only 'now' updates; 'was' is retained.**" | **Confirmed** |
| **PRC-47** | Confluence 04.1.12 | Per-locale currency formatting: symbol position, decimals (incl. zero-decimal), thousand separator, minus placement | Confirmed |
| **PRC-08 / PRC-33** | Confluence 04.1.12 | Price display consistent across PLP, PDP, mini-bag, cart, wishlist, recommended tiles, checkout, order history | Confirmed |
| **PRC-12** | Confluence 04.1.12 | Final sale flag on products. `.docs`: *"No final-sale icon in design yet"* | Confirmed (design pending) |

### 6.1 🔴 REG-042 is a confirmed requirement with no AC

> "If price changes again after being put on sale, only 'now' updates; 'was' is retained."

This is **Confirmed** in three separate PRD files and is a real behavioural rule about which value populates the Was slot. **It is not covered by any of SFCC-194's four ACs**, and PR #68's description doesn't mention it. PR #68 derives `wasPrice` from `getPriceData`'s `listPrice` — whether that satisfies REG-042 depends on whether SFCC's `listPrice` retains the pre-sale value across a subsequent price change, which is a data-layer question, not a front-end one.

**→ Needs confirming: is REG-042 satisfied by SFCC pricebook behaviour, or does it need explicit front-end handling?**

### 6.2 🔴 PRC-18 contradicts itself and PRC-17 across sources

| Source | Says |
|---|---|
| Confluence 04.1.12, **PRC-17** | "Discounts will **not apply to products already on sale** or to gift cards." |
| Confluence 04.1.12, **PRC-18** | "Customer group discounts will **prevail over** sale pricing." |
| `.docs/prd/pricing-currency-globale.md:73` (PRC-18, *revised per DR*) | "Customer group discounts **do NOT stack** on sale items… a Gold VIC customer… gets the sale price only — no extra 10% on top." |
| **SFCC-778** AC6 | "…views a product already on standard sale… then **the sale price is displayed and no additional catalogue promotion discount is applied**." |

Three of four agree (sale price wins); Confluence PRC-18's "prevail over sale pricing" is the outlier and contradicts PRC-17 **on the same page**. Not blocking for SFCC-194 itself (no customer-group logic here), but it **is** blocking for SFCC-778, which SFCC-194 gates. Worth raising now rather than at SFCC-778 refinement.

---

## 7. Separation of concerns — the important part

### 7.1 ⚠️ Epic parentage contradicts both epics' own scope statements

| Epic | Its own scope statement |
|---|---|
| **SFCC-5** (PDP) — *SFCC-194's actual parent* | **Out of Scope:** "Pricing display logic and pricebook setup — **covered in SFCC-18 (Pricing)**" |
| **SFCC-18** (Pricing) — status **To Do** | **In Scope:** "**Sale/markdown pricing display (was/now) across PLP, PDP, mini-cart, cart, wishlist, checkout, and order history**" |

Both epics independently agree that Was/Now display belongs to **SFCC-18**. SFCC-194 is parented under **SFCC-5**. Per both epics as written, it is on the wrong epic.

**Why it matters beyond bookkeeping:** PRC-09 requires Was/Now on **eight surfaces** (PLP tiles, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, wishlist, recommended tiles, order history). SFCC-194 delivers one of them. If the price atom is designed as a PDP-local concern it will be rebuilt or forked seven more times; if it's designed as the SFCC-18 shared pricing primitive, the other seven surfaces are mostly composition. The epic assignment quietly decides which of those happens.

### 7.2 ⚠️ Component ownership collision with SFCC-737

**SFCC-737 — `pdp/product-content`** · In Progress · Sprint 4 · assignee **Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz** · linked to SFCC-194 as *"relates to"*.

Its own description is explicit about ownership:

> "The component is a composition container. **It does not own the logic of its child components** — interaction behaviour … are covered in their respective child component stories. This story covers the layout, ordering, and rendering of all child elements within the panel…"

And its ACs claim price as part of its composition contract:
- **AC1** — element order top-to-bottom: "product name + wishlist icon, **price**, product description, colour picker, size selector…"
- **AC4** — "product name, **price**, description, model description, and style code display in the typography styles defined in the design system."

**PR #68 (SFCC-194) modifies `zimmProductContent`** — `index.tsx` and `index.stories.tsx` — adding `originalPrice` and `isPriceLoading` props.

So: **two stories, two developers, same active sprint, same component.** SFCC-737 owns the container's layout/typography contract; SFCC-194 is changing its props. Not necessarily wrong — adding a prop to a composition container is the correct way for a child atom to receive data — but it needs coordinating with Jhoan Rose, because SFCC-737's AC1/AC4 sign-off covers the very element being changed.

### 7.3 Clean boundaries in PR #68 (for the record)

The atom / molecule / page split does follow the project's `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}` structure and the container-vs-presentational rule:

| Layer | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Atom | `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/` | Renders price; `default` + `sale` variants; styling in co-located `.css.ts` recipe |
| Molecule | `ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductContent/` | Forwards `originalPrice` / `isPriceLoading` — no data fetching |
| Mapper | `pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` | Derives `wasPrice` from `listPrice` when `isOnSale` |
| Page/container | `pages/product-detail/index.tsx` | Owns all data fetching + variant resolution |

Styling lives in the recipe, not in component JSX — consistent with the project's styling-layer boundary.

### 7.4 📌 `ZimmProductPrice` is **not** new

PR #68's description says it *"Introduces `ZimmProductPrice` atom (PRC-09)"*. It doesn't — the atom already exists on `develop`:

```
45aaeec  2026-08-26  feat(ui-kits): add PDP static product information atoms and molecules
8d5de1c              feat(pdp): render static product information on the product detail page
4914f30              fix(pdp): consolidate the static product info styling surface and close its test gaps
```

It arrived via **SFCC-89 (PDP UI — Static Product Information)**, merged as PR #64 two days before PR #68 opened. PR #68 **extends** it. Minor, but the PR description overstates what's being introduced, and it means the atom already has an owner story and existing tests/stories to stay compatible with.

---

## 8. Story scope vs. PR #68 scope — the delta

The story is four display ACs. The PR is +415/−118 across 13 files. Mapping what's in the PR back to the ACs:

| PR item | Traces to |
|---|---|
| `ZimmProductPrice` `sale` variant, Was/Now two-span | **AC1** ✅ |
| Branches on presence of `wasPrice`; no sale → single price | **AC2** ✅ |
| Currency formatting per storefront | **AC3** ✅ |
| Sale removed/expired in BM → reverts on next render | **AC4** ✅ |
| **Variant-scoped pricing across 3 URL states** (none / `?color=` / `?pid=`) | ❌ no AC |
| **`masterProductRef` caching of master product for `tieredPrices`** | ❌ no AC |
| **Deep-link fallback for `?pid=` on fresh load** | ❌ no AC |
| **`isPriceStale` guard during variant re-fetch (`keepPreviousData`)** | ❌ no AC |
| **`aria-hidden` fix on the live region** | ❌ no AC (a11y not in this story's ACs) |

The last five are genuinely useful and arguably necessary to make AC1–AC4 *hold* while a shopper switches variants — a Was/Now that goes stale on colour change is a real defect. But none of it is described by the story, it's ~2 points of stated work carrying a page-container refactor, and it lands in `pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (+93 lines in one hunk), which is where the single unresolved CodeRabbit thread sits (Major / maintainability).

**Candidate framings to decide between:**
1. It's in scope — variant-correct pricing is implied by "the PDP displays" and the ACs are just under-specified. Add ACs retrospectively so QA can verify it.
2. It's a separate concern — variant/URL-state resolution belongs to **SFCC-91 (Colour Swatches & Variation Selection, In Progress)** or **SFCC-92 (Size Selection & Add to Bag)**, and should be split out.

Worth an explicit call rather than letting it ride.

---

## 9. Dependency graph

```
SFCC-5 (Epic: PDP, In Progress)
  └── SFCC-194  PDP – Was/Now Sale Price          [In Progress]  ← this story
        └── SFCC-215  design feedback subtask     [Done]

SFCC-194 ──relates to──► SFCC-737  pdp/product-content        [In Progress, Sprint 4]
SFCC-194 ──BLOCKS─────► SFCC-778  Customer Group Pricing      [In Refinement]

SFCC-778 is also blocked by:
  ├── SFCC-38   Test Customer Group & Promotion Config  [Ready For Review]
  └── SFCC-236  Product Card Shared Component           [Tech design]
```

### 9.1 What SFCC-194 blocking SFCC-778 implies

**SFCC-778 — Customer Group Pricing — Catalogue Price Rule Display** needs Was/Now on **PLP, PDP, cart, and checkout**, plus a promotional label (e.g. *"Private Sale — 20% Off Applied"*). It is explicitly a *different mechanism* — catalogue price rule + login required, vs. SFCC-194's sale pricebook + no login.

So `ZimmProductPrice` will need to support:
- a **second trigger source** (catalogue price rule, not just sale pricebook)
- **four+ surfaces**, not just PDP
- an optional **promotional label** slot
- the **strikethrough** treatment SFCC-778's ACs specify (vs. grey-out here — §4.4)

None of that has to be built now, but the atom's prop shape should not actively preclude it. Currently `originalPrice` is generic enough — good.

### 9.2 Related PDP stories in flight (all Sprint 4, all touching the same panel)

| Key | Summary | Status |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC-737 | `pdp/product-content` | In Progress |
| SFCC-91 | PDP UI — Colour Swatches & Variation Selection | **In Progress** ← overlaps §8 |
| SFCC-89 | PDP UI — Static Product Information | Code Review |
| SFCC-736 | `pdp/drawer` | In Progress (PR #67, draft, conflicting) |
| SFCC-723 | `pdp/hero` | Ready For Review |
| SFCC-92 | PDP — Size Selection & Add to Bag | Ready for Development |
| SFCC-731 | `pdp/gallery` | **Blocked** |
| SFCC-741 | `pdp/notify-me` | **Blocked** |
| SFCC-150 | Coming Soon / Back in Soon / Unavailable | Ready for Development |
| SFCC-101 | Measmerize Widget & Find My Size CTA | Ready For Review |
| SFCC-740 | `pdp/find-in-boutique` | Ready For Review |

---

## 10. Open questions / things to raise

| # | Item | Who decides |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | **Was = greyed out or strikethrough?** SFCC-194 build + approval say grey; 04.2 tracker + SFCC-778 ACs say strikethrough (§4.4) | Design (Dani/Dennis/Rebecca) |
| **B** | **REG-042** — "was is retained if price changes again after sale" is Confirmed but has no AC and isn't addressed in the PR. Satisfied by SFCC pricebook behaviour, or needs FE handling? (§6.1) | BA + Integration |

content.text:
Written to `~/Desktop/SFCC-194-story-notes.md` (344 lines). The story itself is small — **2 points, 4 display-only ACs**. What's around it is not.

## The story

**SFCC-194 — PDP – Was/Now Sale Price** · High · In Progress · Sprint 4 (25 Aug–7 Sep) · Jersey Perez Jr · labels `PRC-09` `PRD-003` `Squad-A`

Four ACs, all display: (1) Was+Now when on sale, Now prominent; (2) single price when not; (3) correct currency per storefront; (4) reverts when the sale is pulled in BM. Description is explicit: *"This story covers the PDP price display only."*

Design is signed off — Dani Rivett, 14 Aug: *"Rebecca has approved the green sale price with the greyed out Was price"* — which closed subtask SFCC-215 (the "green not 100% agreed" one).

## Six things worth your attention

**1. Epic parentage is wrong by both epics' own words.** SFCC-194 sits under SFCC-5 (PDP). SFCC-5's Out-of-Scope says *"Pricing display logic — covered in SFCC-18."* SFCC-18's In-Scope says *"Sale/markdown pricing display (was/now) across PLP, PDP, mini-cart, cart, wishlist, checkout, order history."* They agree with each other and disagree with where the ticket lives. This isn't bookkeeping — PRC-09 wants Was/Now on **eight surfaces**, and the epic assignment quietly decides whether the atom gets built as a PDP-local thing or the shared pricing primitive.

**2. Grey-out vs strikethrough — a real fork.** This story is built to grey-out (per the approval). The 04.2 tracker *and* SFCC-778's ACs both say **strikethrough**. SFCC-194 blocks SFCC-778, so today's decision propagates.

**3. REG-042 is Confirmed, has no AC, and isn't in the PR.** *"If price changes again after being put on sale, only 'now' updates; 'was' is retained."* It's in three PRD files. The PR derives `wasPrice` from `listPrice` — whether that retains the pre-sale value across a second price change is an SFCC data question nobody has answered.

**4. The PR is much bigger than the story.** +415/−118 across 13 files. Five significant behaviours have **no AC**: variant-scoped pricing across three URL states, `masterProductRef` caching, `?pid=` deep-link fallback, `isPriceStale` guarding, and the `aria-hidden` live-region fix. They're defensible — stale Was/Now on colour switch is a genuine bug — but they overlap **SFCC-91 (Colour Swatches & Variation Selection, also In Progress)**, and the +93-line hunk in `product-detail/index.tsx` is exactly where the one unresolved CodeRabbit thread sits (Major/maintainability).

**5. Component co-ownership.** PR #68 modifies `zimmProductContent`. That's **SFCC-737**'s component — Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz, In Progress, same sprint — and SFCC-737's AC1/AC4 explicitly claim *price* in its composition and typography contract. Adding props is the right pattern; it just needs a word with Jhoan Rose.

**6. `ZimmProductPrice` isn't new.** The PR says it "introduces" the atom. It landed 26 Aug via SFCC-89/PR #64 (`45aaeec`). This PR extends it.

Two smaller notes: both E2E jobs report **`skipping`**, so there's no E2E evidence for this change; and 04.7 lists no standalone Price component — it's nested under Product Content, still 🟡 *"minor update required"*, while 04.72 says stories shouldn't be signed off until components are locked.

Where do you want to start — the unresolved CodeRabbit thread, or the scope question in §8 first?

- `textStyle` values are registered in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts`. Confirm the exact key used exists.

2. **Multi-part recipe correctness** — the recipe declares `parts: [...]`. Report any structural mismatch — e.g. `baseStyle` defining only SOME parts while variants define others, or a `variants.default: {}` empty object where siblings define all parts.
3. **The bare-token-key guard** — `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` mechanically fails the build on a bare Chakra token key used on a registered scale. input.prompt:
You are reviewing GitHub PR #68 in the repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. The branch `feature/SFCC-194_pdp-was-now-price` is ALREADY CHECKED OUT. Do NOT modify, stage, commit, or check out anything — read-only review.

YOUR SCOPE: **runtime correctness and logic ONLY** — real bugs, silent failures, race conditions, wrong-data-displayed. Another agent covers conventions; another covers styling tokens. Do not report style/naming issues.

This PR implements "Was/Now" sale pricing on the PDP (Salesforce Commerce Cloud PWA Kit). Files to scrutinise, in priority order:
1. overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx  — the big one, ~+101 lines, variant-scoped pricing
2. overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts — the `selectPdpProductInfo` mapper
3. overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx
4. overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductContent/index.tsx
5. overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx
6. overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx

What the PR author claims it does (verify each claim against the code — some may be wrong):
- Derives `wasPrice` from `getPriceData`'s `listPrice` only when `isOnSale` is true AND the list price is a real number.
- Implements variant-scoped pricing using the MASTER product's `variants[]` as the authoritative `tieredPrices` source across three URL states: no selection (falls back to base `priceData`), colour-only (`?color=`), colour+size (`?pid=`).
- A `masterProductRef` caches the master product on first load "so the correct tieredPrices are available after SFCC switches the fetched product to a standalone variant."
- A deep-link fallback for a shopper arriving with `?pid=` already set on a fresh page load, using the standalone variant's own `tieredPrices` from `perPricebook: true`, when `masterProductRef` is empty.
- Guards against stale Was/Now during variant re-fetches via `isPriceStale` (`requestedProductId !== product?.id`), suppressing the price while `keepPreviousData` holds the previous variant's data.

HUNT SPECIFICALLY FOR:
- **A `useRef` that is written during render or never reset.** `masterProductRef` is the prime suspect: what happens when the shopper navigates from product A's PDP to product B's PDP without a full page reload (client-side route change)? Does the ref still hold product A's master? Trace it. A stale master would mean product B shows product A's prices — a serious defect on a luxury retail PDP.
- **Effect dependency arrays** — missing deps, or deps that cause the effect to loop/thrash.
- **The `isOnSale` / `listPrice` derivation** — what if `listPrice === salePrice` (a sale pricebook entry exists but at the same price)? What if `listPrice` is 0, negative, null, undefined, or a string? Does a bogus "Was $0" reach the UI? Read `getPriceData` (find it — likely in the base SFCC package under node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app or an override) and confirm the actual shape and semantics of what it returns, including `isOnSale`, `listPrice`, `currentPrice`, and `tieredPrices`.
- **Bundles / product sets / gift cards** — `getPriceData` behaves differently for these. Does the new code handle or corrupt them?
- **The three URL states** — reason through each concretely and say whether the resolved price is correct. Especially: colour-only selection where multiple sizes have DIFFERENT prices — which price is shown, and is that right?
- **`isPriceStale` correctness** — `requestedProductId !== product?.id`. On the very first load, what are both sides? For a master product with no `pid` param? Could this suppress the price permanently in some state, or fail to suppress when it should?
- **Silent failures / swallowed errors** — a fallback that quietly shows a wrong-but-plausible price is worse than showing nothing. Flag every place a fallback could mask a real data problem.
- **Loading state** — `isLoading` renders an `opacity:0` placeholder containing only a space character. Assess whether the claimed purpose (preserving the layout slot / exact Was-Now dimensions) is actually achieved. Also: for a NON-sale product, the loading branch forces the `sale` variant — is that right?
- **Requirement REG-042** (confirmed project requirement, in .docs/prd/pdp.md and .docs/prd/regional.md): "If price changes again after being put on sale, only 'now' updates; 'was' is retained." Assess whether this implementation can satisfy that, or whether it structurally cannot because of where `wasPrice` is sourced from. Be precise about what you can and cannot determine from the front-end code alone.

METHOD — closed loop, non-negotiable:
- For every finding, construct a CONCRETE failure scenario: specific inputs / URL / navigation sequence → the specific wrong output. A finding without a concrete failure path is not a finding.
- Read the SURROUNDING code, not just the diff — the pre-existing `product-detail/index.tsx` is large; understand how `useProduct`, `keepPreviousData`, the `pid`/`color` URL params, and the existing variant-selection flow already work BEFORE judging the new code.
- Verify against the real `getPriceData` / SDK types in node_modules. Do not guess at API shapes.
- Mark each finding CONFIRMED (you traced it and it definitely breaks) or PLAUSIBLE (needs runtime proof).
- Actively try to DISPROVE your own findings before reporting. If existing code already guards against something, say so and drop the finding.

OUTPUT: Ranked findings, worst first. Each: `file:line` — severity (Blocker / Major / Minor) — the defect in one sentence — CONCRETE failure scenario (inputs → wrong result) — CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE. Then 3 lines on overall logic soundness. No preamble. Do not pad — a short list of real bugs beats a long list of speculation.

YOUR SCOPE: **test and Storybook coverage quality ONLY.** Another agent covers conventions, another styling, another runtime logic. Do not report findings outside testing.

- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.test.tsx  (+51 lines, 8 new tests claimed)
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.stories.tsx (+20)

- overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts

For the most important new assertions, determine whether they would ACTUALLY CATCH a regression:

- Call out any test that is tautological, asserts on a mock rather than behaviour, or would pass even if the feature were removed.

Is there a `Default` export? Are the added stories meaningful states or redundant prop permutations? Is a `play` function warranted here and absent, or correctly omitted?

VERIFY this claim: open `zimmProductContent/index.stories.tsx`, find those three stories, and confirm whether they actually assert an exact child count. Report whether the comment is accurate — it is used to justify a design decision.
5. **E2E** — per testing.md's "Change-scoped E2E" and "BrowserStack story scoping": this PR's CI shows both Playwright and BrowserStack jobs as `skipping`. Determine WHY from the rules + `.github/workflows/qa.yml` logic (is it the area allow-list resolving to `skip`, or no `@SFCC-194`-tagged spec existing?). State whether a spec SHOULD exist for this change and what the consequence of the skip is.
6. **Test-file placement/naming** — `.test.tsx` vs `.test.ts`, co-location, `index.test.*` convention.

METHOD — closed loop:
- Run the actual test files with `npx vitest run <path>` and report the real pass/fail/skip counts you observe, not what the PR description claims (it claims "8 new ZimmProductPrice unit tests" — verify the real number).
- Every finding must cite `file:line` and be verified against the real file.
- Mark CONFIRMED vs PLAUSIBLE.
- Be fair: if the tests are genuinely good, say so. Do not manufacture gaps.

OUTPUT: (a) observed test run results (real numbers). (b) A short verdict per test file: adequate / thin / tautological, with reasons. (c) Ranked gap list: severity (Blocker / Major / Minor) — what is untested — why it matters — CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE. (d) 3-line overall verdict on test adequacy for merge. No preamble.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/code-quality

Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.

---

## Input

The user will provide one of:
- A file path or directory to audit
- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`

If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.

---

## Parallel execution

For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
bundle all checks into one agent.

- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
- **Agent B — Import analysis**
- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**

For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.

---

## Agent A — Naming & structure

Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
that's how the files drift apart.

Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:

- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
  structure**.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.

For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").

---

## Agent B — Import analysis

For each file, read the import statements and check:

- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.

---

## Agent C — TypeScript coverage

Check each file against the relevant rule file:

- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).

Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.

---

## Agent D — Test & story coverage

For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
- For logic-heavy components or hooks: the component's **own** `*.test.ts`/`*.test.tsx` exists
  in the same folder. A `play` function elsewhere (this component's own story, or — this is
  the common miss — a *different* component's assembly-level story) does not substitute for
  it, even when it happens to exercise the same rendered output; see testing.md's note under
  "What to test (and what to skip)". A component's own test file may still mock a hook or
  child component whose internals are covered elsewhere — the point is that the component's
  own render-branch/event-wiring contract has a test discoverable from its own folder.
- If a test file exists, verify:
  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
- If a logic-heavy file has no test file of its own, flag as MISSING TEST — regardless of
  whether a `play` function exists somewhere else in the codebase.

For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
  one-liners are exempt.
- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).

---

## Output format

Combine all agent results into a single prioritised report:

```
## Code Quality Report
**Scope:** [files audited]
**Branch:** [current branch]
**Date:** [today]

### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge
[Issues that would fail review or cause runtime errors — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🟡 Should fix in this PR
[Issues that affect maintainability or violate conventions — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)
[Minor style issues, missing test cases for edge cases — one line per issue]

### ✅ No issues found
[List checks that passed cleanly]

### Summary
X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog items
```

Do not suggest refactors beyond the scope of the changed files.

Decisive result — the committed registry doesn't match a clean regen on its own branch:

| Component | committed in PR | fresh regen | on `develop` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Header | **1** | 13 | 13 |
| Icons | **3** | 7 | 10 |
| Image | **8** | 10 | 10 |
| Field | **31** | 21 | 24 |
| App | **8** | 5 | 5 |

The fresh regen largely reproduces `develop`'s numbers, so `develop` was right and the PR's committed values are junk — regenerated from a dirty/partial state. Working tree restored, no changes left behind.

**Verified so far, first-hand:**
- ✅ `tsc --noEmit` clean · **389/389 tests pass** (25 files) · `audit:tokens` introduces **no** new violations (the 4 failures are all pre-existing in `header/`)
- ❌ **`npm run lint` fails with 6 prettier errors this PR introduced** (`zimmProductContent/index.tsx:45`, `product-detail/index.tsx:364,371,373,942`, `productInfo.test.ts:21`) — plus a **dead `eslint-disable react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`** at `product-detail/index.tsx:402` that lint reports as unnecessary. Lint isn't a CI gate here, which is why the PR is green. The `restrict-template-expressions` warnings and the `routes.tsx`/`recipeGuards.test.ts` errors are pre-existing — not this PR's.
- ❌ **Hardcoded English `Was` / `Now`** at `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:107,110`. The project has an established microcopy pattern the atom bypasses: `useUiCopy` (`overrides/app/hooks/useUiCopy.ts`), documented as safe in presentational leaves and degrading to fallback text with **zero setup** — which is precisely the "usable in Storybook without an intl provider" reason the atom's own comment gives for avoiding intl. Two live precedents: `zimmSubscribeSection/index.tsx:52-56` and `footer/bottomBar/index.tsx:35-36`. Base SFCC's `display-price` localises its labels via `formatMessage`. Against AC3 ("any storefront", 11 locales), a French shopper gets "Was €1.100 Now €1.000".
- ✅ Credit where due: the `chore: add temp priceData debug logs` commit's logging **was** cleaned up — no `console.*` in any changed file. And `masterProductRef` staleness across products **is** guarded (`cachedMasterMatchesCurrent`, `index.tsx:363-366`).

Four reviewers (conventions, styling/tokens, logic, tests) and the CodeRabbit CLI run are still going. I'll hold the verdict until they land and I've verified their claims.

Confirmed and quantified. Correcting one thing I told you earlier:

**The right fix for the hardcoded labels is `intl.formatMessage`, not `useUiCopy`.** The sibling atom in the same folder — `zimmProductStyleCode/index.tsx:34-39` — explicitly rules out `useUiCopy` for exactly this case: `useContentful.ts` requests entries with no `locale` parameter, so it would serve the space default to all 8 storefronts. The reviewed design (cached master + identity guard + fallback) is inert, so the stale-master hazard the guard was written for cannot fire, and equally the fallback offers no protection if `expand: ['variations']` is ever narrowed. **CONFIRMED.**

The `pid`-rewriting effect (`index.tsx:422-425`) starts with `if (!variant) return;`, and `useVariant` returns `undefined` unless exactly one variant matches all params.

URL becomes `?color=Y&size=S&pid=M1`; `useVariant` matches 0 variants so `pid` is **never** replaced. `requestedProductId === 'M1' === product.id` → `isPriceStale === false`; the memo takes the `urlPid` branch and renders colour **X**'s price and Was/Now while the swatches show colour Y selected — persistently, not transiently. Root cause is pre-existing in base, but the new code had the fresh `color` param in hand and chose the stale `pid`. **CONFIRMED.**

**6. `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts:71-74` — Major — `typeof listPrice === 'number'` is the only guard; there is no `currentPrice > 0` or `listPrice > currentPrice` floor, so `getPriceData`'s Infinity→0 reset can surface as "Was $795.00 Now $0.00".**
`findLowestPrice` (`product-utils.js:242-261`) leaves `data: null` and `minPrice: Infinity` when no candidate has a numeric `price`, then resets `minPrice` to **0**. `tieredPrices` then falls through to `product?.tieredPrices` — on the spread object at `index.tsx:399` that is the *master's* tiered prices — so `listPrice` is a real number and `isOnSale: 0 < listPrice` is `true`.

Each span is therefore a blockified flex item whose only content is a single collapsible space; `nowrap` suppresses line breaking but still collapses white-space runs, so each item generates no line box and contributes 0 height — the `<p>` collapses rather than holding the price's line box. `\u00A0`/`&nbsp;` would actually reserve it. So the requirement is satisfied *iff* the merchant only ever edits the sale price book and leaves the list entry alone; if the list entry itself is lowered, the "Was" follows it and the requirement breaks, invisibly to this code. Two things I cannot determine from the front end: whether Zimmermann's BM setup guarantees list-book immutability, and whether a third price book above RRP could ever be in context (which would make `max()` pick that instead of the RRP). Both need a BM/price-book answer, not a code change — but the PR should not be read as *implementing* REG-042.

The two genuine correctness gaps are structural, not incidental: dropping `isRange` turns a legitimate "From" range into a definite Was/Now claim, and preferring the URL's `pid` over its `color` propagates a stale selection that `isPriceStale` cannot see. `isPriceStale` itself is sound as a staleness *detector* — I could not find a state where it suppresses permanently or fails to suppress a cross-product navigation — but it is applied one step too aggressively, blanking a value that is already correct. Sets and bundles are untouched: their `ProductView` instances (`index.tsx:845,871`) pass no `renderHeader`, so `StaticProductHeader` and all of this code are unreachable for them.</result>
